styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Colaba's colonial streets, museums and the Gateway of India.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Street snacks, Irani cafés and long lunches across the city.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Elephanta caves, forts and the story of old Bombay.

stays.why: Walk to the Gateway of India, museums and the ferry wharf. Best first-time base for sights and food.
Central and close to Colaba sights, with metro and train links. Good mix of heritage hotels and business stays.
Cafés, nightlife and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link. Near the domestic airport and BKC business district.
Beach-side stays near the airport. Quieter evenings and easy access to the western suburbs.

food: Try Mumbai street snacks: vada pav, pav bhaji, bhel puri and pani puri. Eat where locals queue; prices are low, often ₹20–100.
Have a meal at an old Irani café: bun maska, chai and keema. Cheap and full of character.
Seafood is a highlight: try a thali or fish curry at a local restaurant. Ask about spice level.
Vegetarian food is easy to find everywhere, from thali places to upscale restaurants.
Drink bottled or filtered water. Go easy on very spicy food on your first day.
more_time: Take a ferry from Ferry Wharf to Elephanta Island for the cave temples; check sailing times on the day.
Spend a half day in Bandra: cafés, street art and the sea link views.
Add a day trip to a nearby beach or hill area; ask your hotel about current transport options.

recommend.why: Two nights covers Colaba, the Gateway, Elephanta and a food crawl; add a night for Bandra and the suburbs.

month_notes: January: dry and mild, highs near 29°C. Great for walking and sightseeing.
February: dry and warm, around 31°C. Comfortable days, cool evenings.
March: dry and hotter, up to 32°C. Start sightseeing early.
April: hot at 33°C and dry. Carry water and plan indoor breaks.
May: hot and humid, a few rain days. Pre-monsoon showers can appear.
June: monsoon starts; heavy rain on most days. Pack rain gear and expect delays.
July: wettest month, rain almost daily. Indoor sights and cafés are best.
August: still very wet. Flooding is possible; check conditions before going out.
September: rain continues but eases late in the month. Carry an umbrella.
October: rain tapers off; warmer and drier days return.
November: dry and pleasant, around 32°C. A good month to visit.
December: dry and mild, highs near 31°C. Busy season; book hotels early.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical monsoon climate: hot and humid most of the year, with a long, very wet monsoon from June to September.

items.title: Best time: November to March
items.text: Dry days around 29–32°C with cooler evenings. Ideal for walking, ferries and street food.

items.title: Monsoon: June to September
items.text: Rain on most days, heaviest in July and August. Expect wet streets and possible travel delays.

items.title: Hot and humid April to May
items.text: Highs near 33°C with rising humidity. Sightsee early morning and rest in the afternoon.

items.title: Carry rain gear in monsoon
items.text: An umbrella or light raincoat is essential from June to September.

items.title: Humidity all year
items.text: It feels hotter than the numbers. Light, breathable clothes help.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light cotton clothes, comfortable walking shoes, sunscreen and a hat; add rain gear for the monsoon months.

transit.best: Use the metro and local trains for speed; Uber or Ola for door-to-door trips.

modes.text: Modern and fast. The Aqua Line links the airport to BKC and Colaba.
Suburban 'local' trains are the city's artery. Buy a ₹275 Tourist Ticket for first class all day.
Cheap and everywhere. Use the m-Indicator app to plan routes.
Metered black-and-yellow taxis and blue cabs are common; agree the fare or insist on the meter. Uber and Ola work well.
Ferries from Ferry Wharf reach Elephanta Island and nearby beaches.
Not practical for most visitors; traffic is heavy and parking is hard. Use taxis and trains instead.
Good in Colaba and Fort for sights. Use transport for longer trips, especially in heat or rain.
